# opnsense_dnsmasq_domain (Resource)

Dnsmasq domain overrides send queries for a domain to a specific DNS server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opnsense_dnsmasq_domain" "consul" {
  domain = "service.consul"
  ip     = "10.0.118.10"
  port   = 8600
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Domain to override, e.g. `corp.example.com`.
- `ip` (String) IP address of the DNS server queries are forwarded to.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description here for your reference (not parsed).
- `firewall_alias` (String) Firewall alias filled with the addresses resolved for this domain (ipset).
- `port` (Number) Port of that DNS server. Defaults to `-1` (OPNsense default).
- `sequence` (Number) Order in which overrides are evaluated. Defaults to `1`.
- `source_ip` (String) Source address used to reach the server.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the dnsmasq domain override.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import opnsense_dnsmasq_domain using the `id`. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = opnsense_dnsmasq_domain.example
  id = "<opnsense-resource-id>"
}
```

Using `terraform import`, import opnsense_dnsmasq_domain using the `id`. For example:

```console
% terraform import opnsense_dnsmasq_domain.example <opnsense-resource-id>
```
